title: Avoiding Reverse Falls in Drainage Piping
description: One of the most common mistakes in drainage installation is failing to maintain a consistent downward slope, resulting in a reverse fall or 'belly' in the pipe. When gravity flow is compromised by improper support or settlement, wastewater and solids pool in low spots rather than discharging fully. Over time, these stagnant areas accumulate buildup and lead to recurring clogs and slow drains. Professional installation requires verifying grade continuously using a proper level and securing pipe supports at regular intervals specified by the manufacturer and local code to prevent sagging.

Avoiding Reverse Falls in Drainage Piping

One of the most common mistakes in drainage installation is failing to maintain a consistent downward slope, resulting in a reverse fall or 'belly' in the pipe. When gravity flow is compromised by improper support or settlement, wastewater and solids pool in low spots rather than discharging fully. Over time, these stagnant areas accumulate buildup and lead to recurring clogs and slow drains. Professional installation requires verifying grade continuously using a proper level and securing pipe supports at regular intervals specified by the manufacturer and local code to prevent sagging.
